title: Keep the air flowing
summary: Can you scan a crater and keep the habitat breathing?
goal: Finish 3 shifts with air and power above zero. Complete a science scan.
terms: A machine that helps keep cabin air safe.
Stored energy that runs the outpost.
When a choice helps one thing but costs another.

reflection.question: What did the crater scan cost the air system?
answers: It used power and delayed a chance to recycle air.
The crater itself used up oxygen.
reflection.explain: The scan shared the battery with the air recycler. The crater did not consume oxygen.

choices.label: Run air recycler
choices.description: Give the crew a healthier air reserve.

choices.label: Scan the crater
choices.description: Collect science now; the recycler waits.

delayed.reason: The scan used power and time that could have run the air recycler.

choices.description: Keep systems running while the battery refills.

title: Storm watch
summary: A space-weather alert changes the plan.
goal: Finish 3 shifts safely and complete an indoor experiment or survey.
terms: A burst of energy from the Sun.
Material placed between a crew and radiation.
A game index, not a radiation dose.

reflection.question: Why might a crew postpone an outdoor survey?
answers: Shelter can reduce risk during a possible solar particle event.
A flare record tells us the exact dose at this Moon base.
reflection.explain: Space-weather information can change plans. This archived flare does not measure our fictional base.

choices.label: Move into shelter
choices.description: Protect the crew; research waits one shift.

choices.description: Improve shielding during a work period.

choices.label: Continue outdoor survey
choices.description: Gather science, then face a later safety cost.

delayed.reason: The crew stayed outside in this modeled storm scenario.

choices.label: Restore power
choices.description: Air reserve falls while the battery refills.

title: Grow the next meal
summary: A sealed grow box needs water, light, and time.
goal: Finish 4 shifts with food at least 25, water above zero, and a safe crew.
terms: A controlled place with light and water for plants.
Food collected when a crop is ready.
Messages between Earth and the Moon take time; this game simplifies the wait.

reflection.question: Why can a bigger crop plan be risky?
answers: It uses more water and power before food arrives.
Plants grow instantly without needing supplies.
reflection.explain: A harvest arrives later. The crew still needs resources while it grows.

choices.label: Grow leafy greens
choices.description: Moderate cost, harvest in two shifts.

delayed.reason: The sealed grow box produced leafy greens after two shifts.

choices.label: Conserve supplies
choices.description: Save water and power; the small harvest runs short.

delayed.reason: The small grow plan produced too little food for the crew.

choices.label: Use the large grow box
choices.description: A larger harvest arrives after three shifts.

delayed.reason: The larger grow box finally produced a harvest.

choices.label: Ask Earth for advice

delayed.reason: Earth's reply arrived: protect the water supply and keep enough light for the crop.

choices.label: Decide locally
